findings.summary: Page titles run one chapter behind the material each page actually teaches, from page 2 through page 4.
findings.evidence: Page 2 is titled "Why Caching Exists & Where Caches Live (cont.)" but its body is chapter 2 ("The Control Surface", "Lifetime Directives", `max-age`/`s-maxage`/`Age`, `public`/`private`/`no-store`); page 3 is titled "Freshness: Cache-Control Lifetime Directives" but teaches "What A Validator Is" / "ETag" / "Last-Modified"; page 4 is titled "Validators: ETag and Last-Modified" but teaches "Conditional Headers", "The Two Answers" and "Write-Side Twins". Page 5 ("Stale Serving") realigns, so only 2–4 are offset.
findings.fix: Retitle page 2 to "Freshness: Cache-Control Lifetime Directives", page 3 to "Validators: ETag and Last-Modified", page 4 to "Revalidation: The Conditional Request Dance", and move the leading spillover blocks (the fresh/stale QA onto page 1; the "Read The Three Correctly" sidebox and "Three defaults to memorise" callout onto page 2; the "Hash at build time" callout onto page 3) so each page opens on the chapter its title names.

findings.summary: The deck stops at chapter 7 while its own caption promises ten pages ending in a CDN chapter, a mistakes chapter and a cheat sheet.
findings.evidence: Caption: "10 pages on how HTTP caching actually works: freshness math, ETags vs Last-Modified, the conditional request dance, Vary as a hit-rate landmine, immutable assets, CDN precedence, and the mistakes that pin bad bytes on real browsers for a year. Ends with a cheat sheet you can paste straight into your config." The slides array holds 7 pages and ends on "Immutable Assets & Cache Busting"; no CDN, trade-offs, mistakes or cheat-sheet page exists.
findings.fix: Either add the three missing chapters (CDN Behaviour, Trade-offs/Cost Models, Common Mistakes + Cheat Sheet) or rewrite the caption to describe the seven pages actually shipped and drop the "CDN precedence", "mistakes" and "cheat sheet" promises.

findings.summary: The caption promises a 10-page deck but only 7 page titles exist, and two of the topics it advertises (CDN precedence, the pasteable cheat sheet) have no corresponding title.
findings.evidence: Caption: "10 pages on how HTTP caching actually works: ... CDN precedence ... Ends with a cheat sheet you can paste straight into your config." — titles array contains 7 entries, ending at "Immutable Assets & Cache Busting" with no CDN or cheat-sheet page.
findings.fix: Either add the missing pages (CDN precedence, common mistakes, cheat sheet) to reach 10, or change the caption to "7 pages" and drop the "CDN precedence" and "Ends with a cheat sheet" claims so the promise matches the deck.

findings.summary: "Origin shield" and "PoP" are used as load-bearing terms on pages 1 and 5 but are never defined anywhere in the deck, because the CDN chapter that defines them is absent.
findings.evidence: Page 1 flow nodes: ["memory cache","disk cache","SW Cache API","CDN edge","origin shield","origin"] and card line "CDN edge PoP"; page 5 stampede table row ["origin shield","one tier absorbs"] offers it as a defence with no prior definition.
findings.fix: Add a one-line gloss at first use on page 1 — e.g. "origin shield: one designated mid-tier cache that fronts the origin so many edges produce one miss" and expand PoP to "point of presence" — or drop both terms from pages 1 and 5 until the CDN chapter ships.

findings.summary: The lifetime table and the flowchart both classify `Expires` and `Age` as Cache-Control directives, teaching a false taxonomy right where the reader is learning the header's structure.
findings.evidence: Table headers ["Directive","Who obeys","Effect"] with rows ["`Expires`","all caches","HTTP/1.0 date, loses to `max-age`"] and ["`Age`","set by shared","seconds already sat in cache"]; the flowchart rooted at node "Cache-Control" puts "Expires" under the "lifetime" branch beside "max-age" and "s-maxage".
findings.fix: Rename the table's first column to "Header / directive" and mark the two rows as standalone headers, and remove the "Expires" node from the Cache-Control flowchart (it belongs in the "Legacy Headers" bullets already on the same page).

findings.summary: Page titles are shifted one chapter behind their content, so slides 3 and 4 are labelled with the wrong topic.
findings.evidence: Slide 3 is titled "Freshness: Cache-Control Lifetime Directives" but its blocks are "What A Validator Is", "ETag", "Last-Modified", "Generating ETags"; slide 4 is titled "Validators: ETag and Last-Modified" but its blocks are "When Stale Hits", "Conditional Headers", "The Two Answers" (304/200/412). The lifetime directives (`max-age`, `s-maxage`, `Expires`, `Age`) actually sit on slide 2, titled "Why Caching Exists & Where Caches Live (cont.)".
findings.fix: Re-title slide 2 "Freshness: Cache-Control Lifetime Directives", slide 3 "Validators: ETag and Last-Modified", slide 4 "Conditional Requests and 304", and re-check the in-text cross-references ("(ch 6)" for Vary, "(ch 5)" for stale serving) against the corrected chapter numbering.

findings.summary: The Cardinality Killers table overflows its sticky note, with the Verdict column hanging past the card's right border.
findings.evidence: Header "Verdict" and cells "catastrophe", "use private" and "full opt-out" sit outside the pink/green note boundary, drawn directly over the background.
findings.fix: Reduce the table to fit the card width (narrow the Verdict column or shorten labels) or widen the note so all three columns render inside it.

findings.summary: The Two-Tier Policy table is wider than its sticky note, so the Cache-Control values are cut off at the card edge and the table rules bleed onto the corkboard background.
findings.evidence: Row 'HTML (alt)' shows "max-age=0, must-revalidat" and row 'hashed asset' shows "max-age=31536000, immutabl" — the trailing characters of "must-revalidate" and "immutable" are clipped, and horizontal rules continue past the note's right border toward the page edge.
findings.fix: Shrink the table's font/column widths or widen the card so the longest value "max-age=31536000, immutable" fits inside the note, and clip the table to the card bounds.

findings.summary: The caption advertises a page count and a closing cheat sheet that this deck does not contain.
findings.evidence: Caption: "10 pages on how HTTP caching actually works ... Ends with a cheat sheet you can paste straight into your config." The `slides` array holds 7 slides covering 6 chapters, and the last block is the "white screen at deploy" callout — there is no cheat-sheet slide.
findings.fix: Correct the count to match the shipped slides and either add the closing config cheat-sheet slide or drop that sentence from the caption.

findings.summary: The cache hierarchy diagram places the service worker Cache API after the HTTP disk cache, reversing the real lookup order.
findings.evidence: Slide 1 flow: "memory cache", "disk cache", "SW Cache API", "CDN edge", "origin shield", "origin". A service worker's `fetch` handler intercepts the request before the HTTP disk cache is consulted (only the in-memory cache short-circuits ahead of it — a disk-cache hit still fires the SW fetch event).
findings.fix: Reorder the nodes to "memory cache", "SW Cache API", "disk cache", "CDN edge", "origin shield", "origin".

findings.summary: "TTL" is used on four pages and never expanded or defined.
findings.evidence: Page 1 sidebox: "You never chose that TTL and cannot see it"; later "refresh headers, restart TTL" (page 4), "jittered TTL" (page 5), "keep old assets 1 TTL" (page 7).
findings.fix: On first use in the Heuristic Freshness sidebox, write "time to live (TTL) — the freshness lifetime" so the abbreviation is anchored before it recurs.

findings.summary: `must-revalidate` is explained by its effect on stale-on-error fallbacks, a mechanism not introduced until page 5, with no cross-reference.
findings.evidence: Page 2 bullet: "`must-revalidate` kills stale-on-error fallbacks" — `stale-if-error` is first defined on page 5; the neighbouring QA block on the same page does carry a pointer ("Or be explicitly allowed to serve stale (ch 5)").
findings.fix: Append the same pointer: "`must-revalidate` kills stale-on-error fallbacks (ch 5)".

findings.summary: The claim that the origin chooses between the two validators is wrong and contradicts the spec rule stated on the next page.
findings.evidence: Slide 3: "Send both when you can / Clients echo both back on revalidation / The origin picks the cheaper comparison" — but slide 4 correctly states "Both sent? Origin MUST use `If-None-Match`, ignore the date", which is RFC 9110 §13.1.3 ("A recipient MUST ignore If-Modified-Since if the request contains an If-None-Match header field").
findings.fix: Replace "The origin picks the cheaper comparison" with "If both come back, `If-None-Match` wins — `If-Modified-Since` MUST be ignored".

findings.summary: The inline code string in the 'Three defaults to memorise' note runs into the card's right border and the final character is clipped.
findings.evidence: "max-age=31536000, immutable" ends flush against the red card border, rendering as "immutabl" + partial letter.
findings.fix: Allow the code span to wrap, or reduce its font size so the full "immutable" token sits inside the card padding.

findings.summary: The table headed "The Two Answers" lists three rows and introduces 412 before the section that explains it.
findings.evidence: Heading "The Two Answers" over rows ["304",...], ["200",...], ["412","empty","write rejected"]; 412 is only explained two blocks later under "Write-Side Twins" ("`412 Precondition Failed` = someone else wrote first").
findings.fix: Drop the 412 row from the table (leaving the two answers a conditional GET can get) and let 412 appear first in the "Write-Side Twins" bullets, or retitle the table "Conditional Responses" and move it after the write-side section.

findings.summary: The page's closing payoff rests on `immutable`, which is not defined until page 7, with no forward pointer.
findings.evidence: Page 4 callout: "A 304 still costs a full round trip. Revalidation buys bandwidth only — which is exactly why `immutable` assets matter."
findings.fix: Add the deck's existing cross-reference style: "...why `immutable` assets matter (ch 7)".

findings.summary: The directive name in the stale-while-revalidate note runs past the note's right padding into the border.
findings.evidence: "stale-while-revalidate=N" terminates exactly on the card's right edge, with the trailing "N" overlapping the border before the line wraps to "— serve stale now".
findings.fix: Enable wrapping mid-token for long code spans or reduce the code font size so the directive fits within the card's inner width.

findings.summary: The stated reload penalty for omitting `immutable` is Firefox-specific and misleading for Chrome and Safari.
findings.evidence: Slide 7: "`immutable` = do not revalidate, even on reload / Without it a plain refresh still fires `If-None-Match` / That is one wasted RTT per asset, per reload". Chrome (since v55) enforces cache-miss only on the main document on a normal reload and does not revalidate fresh subresources at all — which is why Chrome never shipped support for `immutable`; Firefox kept the revalidating reload and added `immutable` (Firefox 49) as the opt-out.
findings.fix: Qualify it: "Firefox revalidates long-lived subresources on a normal reload unless `immutable` is set; Chrome and Safari already skip subresource revalidation on reload, so `immutable` is a no-op there."
